Rashi on Megillah 7b:10:1.hebrew: אין בין יום טוב לשבת - להיות מותר לכתחלה ביום טוב מה שאסור בשבת, אבל לענין עונשין יש הרבה, שזה בסקילה ובכרת, וזה בלאו גרידא:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:10:1.english: There is no [difference] between a Festival and Shabbat - [That is,] for what is forbidden on Shabbat to be permitted from the outset on a Festival; however, regarding punishments there are many [differences], for this [Shabbat] is [punishable] by stoning and by karet [excision], whereas this [a Festival] is merely [a violation of] a negative commandment:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:11:1.english: This and that are equal - [they are] prohibited on a Festival just as on Shabbat:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:15:1.english: [In which] it is possible - For example, a knife that became nicked on the Festival eve:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:15:2.english: [In] which it is impossible - For example, a knife that became nicked on the Festival:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:16:1.hebrew: בידי אדם - יש בה מיתת ב"ד:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:16:1.english: At the hand of Man - It [i.e., Shabbat] carries the death penalty of a court:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:18:1.english: So too, [regarding] Yom Kippur, he is liable with his life - for a prohibition [punishable by] karet [excision] is like a court-imposed death penalty:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:18:2.hebrew: ופטורים מלשלם - אם הדליק גדישו של חבירו ביום הכפורים, שאין תשלומין אצל חיוב מיתה, שנאמר: "ולא יהיה אסון ענש יענש" (שמות כא) — הא אם יהיה אסון, לא יענש:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:18:2.english: And they are exempt from paying - [That is,] if one set fire to his fellow's stack of grain on Yom Kippur, for there is no [obligation of] monetary payment alongside liability for the death penalty, as it is stated: "And if there be no fatality, he shall surely be fined" (Exodus 21[:22]) — [implying that] if there is a fatality, he shall not be fined.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:19:1.hebrew: כל חייבי כריתות שלקו - שהתרו בהן עדים על לאו שעמו כרת, ולקו בבית דין:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:19:1.english: All [those] liable to karet who were flogged - [meaning] that witnesses warned them regarding a negative commandment that carries karet, and they were flogged in court:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:19:2.english: They were exempted from their karet - the Heavenly court no longer exacts punishment [from them]:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג קיימת בנו רבינו ומשלוח מנות - דהא תרי מנות איכא:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:1:1.english: This is the correct reading: “You have fulfilled through us, our teacher: ‘And sending portions’” - For behold, there are two portions [here].

Rashi on Megillah 7b:20:1.english: We learned - that [Shabbat and Yom Kippur] are distinct:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:20:2.hebrew: ואם איתא - דנפטרו, אידי ואידי בידי אדם הוא: אף ביום הכפורים יש מלקות על לאו שבו, ובית דין פוטרין אותו מכרת:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:20:2.english: And if it is so - that they are exempted [from karet through lashes], [then] both this [case] and that [case] are at the hand of Man: even on Yom Kippur there are lashes for its negative prohibition, and the court [thereby] exempts him from karet.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:1.hebrew: אמר רב נחמן - לעולם אינן חלוקין עליו חביריו, והא דקתני דאין זדונו בידי אדם:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:1.english: Rav Nachman said - In truth, his colleagues do not disagree with him; and [as for] that which [the Mishnah] teaches that its intentional transgression is not [punished] by human hands:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:2.hebrew: הא מני ר' יצחק היא - דאמר במסכת מכות דאין מלקין בלאו הניתן לאזהרת כרת, אפילו התרו בו למלקות, ויליף טעמיה מהאי קרא:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:2.english: Whose [opinion] is this? It is [that of] Rabbi Yitzchak - who said in Tractate Makkot that we do not administer lashes for a negative commandment given as a warning for karet [excision], even if they warned him for lashes, and he derives his reasoning from this verse:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:3.hebrew: כל חייבי כריתות - של עריות, היו בכלל "ונכרתו הנפשות העושות וגו'" שכתוב בפרשת עריות (ויקרא י״ח:כ״ט):
Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:3.english: All those liable to karet - [that is, those] of forbidden sexual relations, were included in [the verse,] "and the souls that do [them] shall be cut off, etc.," which is written in the passage of forbidden sexual relations (Leviticus 18:29):

Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:4.hebrew: למה יצאת כרת באחותו - דכתיב בקדושים תהיו: "ואיש כי יקח את אחותו" וגו':
Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:4.english: Why was karet regarding his sister singled out - For it is written in [the Torah portion] Kedoshim Tihyu: "And if a man shall take his sister, etc." [Leviticus 20:17].

Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:5.hebrew: לדונה בכרת ולא במלקות - אם התרו בהן. ואף על גב דנדה נמי נשנית באותה פרשה, לדבר שנתחדש בה נשנית — להעראה:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:21:5.english: To sentence her to karet and not to lashes - [This applies] if they warned them. And even though [the prohibition of] niddah [a menstruant] was also repeated in that same section, it was repeated for a new matter that was innovated regarding it — [namely,] for ha'ara'ah [the initial stage of intercourse].

Rashi on Megillah 7b:22:1.hebrew: אפילו תימא רבנן היא - דאמרי מלקות אצל כרת, ואפילו הכא ליכא למילף מינה שחלוקין על רבי חנניה. והכי קאמר מתניתין: שבת — עיקר חומר זדונו בידי אדם, וזה — עיקר חומר זדונו בהכרת; ומיהו אם התרו בו ולקה — מיפטר:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:22:1.english: Even [if] you say it is [the view of] the Rabbis - who say [that] lashes [apply] alongside karet, and even so, one cannot derive from it that they disagree with Rabbi Chananya. And this is what the Mishnah means: Shabbat — the primary severity of its intentional [desecration] is at the hand of man, and this [one, Yom Kippur] — the primary severity of its intentional [desecration] is with karet; however, if they warned him and he was flogged, he is exempt [from karet]:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:1.hebrew: הדר שלח ליה איהו - לא גרסינן ליה הכא:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:1.english: He then sent to him - We do not read it here.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:2.english: A sack of dates - A sack full of dates.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:3.hebrew: דאבשונא - שנתייבשו החטים בתנור בעודן כרמל, וקמח שלהן מתוק לעולם:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:3.english: Of roasted [grain] - In which the wheat was dried in an oven while still fresh ears, and its flour is always sweet.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:4.english: Abaye said to him - To Rabba.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:5.english: Now Mari will say - Now Mari will say about you:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:6.hebrew: אי חקלאה מלכא ליהוי דיקולא מצואריה לא נחית - הסל שהיה רגיל להוליך בעודנו בן כפר ומאכיל לבהמתו — לא יוריד עתה מראשו. כך אתה: נעשית מלך וראש בפומבדיתא, ואינך שולח לו אלא דברים המצויין לכל:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:2:6.english: [Even] if a farmer becomes king, the basket does not descend from his neck - The basket that he was accustomed to carry while he was a villager and feed his animal [from it], he will not lower now from his head. So too with you: You have become king and head in Pumbedita, yet you send him only items that are common to all.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:4:1.hebrew: כי נפקי מבי מר - כשיצאתי מבית אדוני רבה לילך לבית אבא מרי בר מר, הייתי שבע:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:4:1.english: When I left the house of the master - When I left the house of my master, Rabba, to go to the house of Abba Marei bar Mar, I was satiated.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:4:2.english: Plates - Bowls of kinds of food.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:4:3.hebrew: דאיכסייא לצעא בתראי - הייתי חפץ לכוס הקערה אחריו. כל אכילה שלא כדרכה נקרא כוסס:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:4:3.english: That I would chew the plate after it - I desired to chew the bowl after it. Any eating that is not in its usual manner is called koseis [chewing].

Rashi on Megillah 7b:5:1.english: Room for a sweet thing is found - Room is found for a sweet thing inside the intestines.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:6:1.hebrew: מחלפי סעודתייהו - זה אוכל עם זה בפורים של שנה זו, ובשניה סועד חברו עמו:
Rashi on Megillah 7b:6:1.english: Would exchange their meals - This one would eat with that one on Purim of this year, and in the second [year], his fellow would dine with him.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:7:1.english: To become intoxicated - To become intoxicated with wine.

Rashi on Megillah 7b:8:1.english: And they became intoxicated - they became drunk:

Rashi on Megillah 7b:9:1.english: It grew dark and the Sages did not come - The day grew late, and the students did not come to the study hall:

Tosafot on Megillah 7b:10:1.hebrew: אין בין יו"ט לשבת - צריך לומר דה"פ: אין שום מלאכה אסורה לשבת שלא תהא אסורה ליום טוב אלא אוכל נפש בלבד, אבל שאר חלוקים יש ביניהן, שזה בסקילה וזה בלאו:
Tosafot on Megillah 7b:10:1.english: There is no [difference] between a Festival and Shabbat - One must say that this is its explanation: there is no labor prohibited on Shabbat that is not prohibited on a Festival, except [for the preparation of] food alone; however, there are other differences between them, for this one [Shabbat] is [punishable] by stoning, and that one [a Festival] is [a violation of] a negative commandment:

Tosafot on Megillah 7b:15:1.hebrew: אן במכשירין שאי אפשר לעשות מערב יו"ט - משמע מדלא פליגי אלא במכשירין, מכלל דגוף המאכל שרי לעשות ביום טוב, אע"ג דאפשר לעשות מערב יו"ט; ומדרבי יהודה נשמע לרבנן, דהא לא פליגי עליה אלא במכשירין. וא"כ קשיא דאמר בפרק המצניע (שבת דף צה. ושם): החולב והמגבן והמחבץ והרודה חלות דבש — בשבת חייב חטאת, הזיד ביו"ט לוקה את הארבעים, אע"ג דהוי אוכל נפש! ואפי' לרבנן דאמרי התם "אחד זה ואחד זה אין בו אלא משום שבות", מ"מ מודו היכא דאיכא אב מלאכה דלוקה. ויש לומר דודאי אוכל נפש המתקלקל אם עושהו מאתמול — מותר לעשות ביו"ט; אבל אוכל נפש דעדיף טפי כשהוא עשוי מאתמול, כגון ההוא דהמצניע — אסור לעשותו ביו"ט. אבל מכשירין, דלא מתקלקל כשנעשו מאתמול, בהא ודאי יש לחלק [בין] היכא דאפשר ללא אפשר:
Tosafot on Megillah 7b:15:1.english: [Here,] to preparatory acts in which it is impossible to perform [them] on the Festival eve - This implies that since they only disagree regarding preparatory acts, by implication it is permitted to prepare the food itself on the Festival, even though it was possible to prepare [it] on the Festival eve — and from Rabbi Yehuda we may infer [the view of] the Rabbis, since they only disagree with him regarding preparatory acts. And if so, this is difficult [in light of] what [the Mishnah] says in the chapter [entitled] Hamatzni'a (Shabbat 95a and there): One who milks, curdles [milk for cheese], churns, or detaches honeycombs — on Shabbat he is liable for a sin-offering, [and] if he did so intentionally on a Festival, he receives forty lashes — even though it is [a case of] food preparation (*okhel nefesh*)! And even according to the Rabbis, who say there, "Both this and that are only [prohibited] because of a rabbinic decree (*shevut*)," nevertheless they agree [that] where there is a primary category of labor (*av melakha*), he receives lashes. And one can say that certainly food that spoils if one prepares it from the day before is permitted to be prepared on the Festival; whereas food that is even better when it is prepared from the day before — such as that [case] in [the chapter] Hamatzni'a — is forbidden to be prepared on the Festival. However, [regarding] preparatory acts, which do not spoil when they are performed from the day before, in this [case] there is certainly [reason] to distinguish between where it is possible [to do them before the Festival] and where it is not possible:

Tosafot on Megillah 7b:21:1.hebrew: חייבי כריתות בכלל היו - פירוש הקונטרס: בכלל "ונכרתו הנפשות העושות". וקשה, דאם כן הוי ליה למימר "אחותו בכלל היתה", כלומר בכלל "ונכרתו הנפשות", ולא היה לו לכתוב כרת בה. ויש לומר דהכי פירושו: "חייבי כריתות בכלל היו" — פירוש, בכלל המלקיות, דבכל אחת ואחת יש לאו; ולמה יצאת כרת באחותו בלא לאו, שהרי הכרת לא איצטריך, שהרי היתה בכלל "ונכרתו"? אלא ודאי יצתה לדונה בכרת, ומינה נגמר לכל האחרים, כדין דבר שהיה בכלל:
Tosafot on Megillah 7b:21:1.english: Those liable to receive karet were included in the general rule - Rashi explained: [They were] included in “and the persons that commit [them] shall be cut off.” And this is difficult: for if so, [the baraita] should have said, “His sister was included in the general rule” — meaning, included in “the persons... shall be cut off” — and [Scripture] should not have written karet regarding her [separately]. One can answer that this is its explanation: “Those liable to receive karet were included in the general rule” — meaning, in the general rule of lashes, for in each and every one [of the forbidden relationships] there is a negative commandment. And why was karet singled out regarding his sister without a negative commandment, given that the [mention of] karet was unnecessary, as she was already included in “shall be cut off”? Rather, she was certainly singled out to sentence her to karet [alone], and from her we derive [this law] for all the others, in accordance with the principle of something that was included in a general rule:

Tosafot on Megillah 7b:7:1.hebrew: דלא ידע בין ארור המן לברוך מרדכי - [בירושלמי]: ארורה זרש, ברוכה אסתר, ארורים כל הרשעים, ברוכים כל היהודים:
Tosafot on Megillah 7b:7:1.english: "That he does not know between cursed is Haman and blessed is Mordecai" - [In the Jerusalem Talmud]: "Cursed is Zeresh, blessed is Esther, cursed are all the wicked, blessed are all the Jews."
